# BitterGit Public Context

## Product Sentence

BitterGit is an open-source, self-hosted Git service for AI coding agents. It
gives every app an ordinary Git repository from the beginning without making a
GitHub account part of setup.

## Motivation

Bitter is meant to remove the setup between an idea and a capable coding agent
getting to work. For someone who does not already use GitHub, creating and
connecting another account before the first repository exists is an avoidable
obstacle.

BitterGit keeps source compatible with standard Git tools. GitHub and other
providers can be imported or connected later as external sources or mirrors;
they are options, not prerequisites.

## Open-Source Alpha

The Apache-2.0 server available at
`https://github.com/sheetgenius/bittergit` provides:

- Git smart HTTP through the system `git-http-backend`
- repository-scoped read, write, and ref controls
- ref events, diff, checkpoints, restore, and export
- conservative folder, zip, and Git import review
- optional external mirrors
- source-linked records tied to exact commits
- optional account, workcell, agent, secret, and deploy integration contracts

The current alpha can be run locally today. It is not yet a hardened public
multi-tenant forge. Keep the demo path on loopback, maintain independent
backups, and read the public security model before a network deployment.

## Place In Bitter

Bitter is a prepared workspace and CLI for agentic coding. BitterGit owns the
source-custody layer: the repository, scoped agent access, recoverable history,
and exact commit behind later work.

The wider hosted direction is:

```text
Idea -> Bitter app -> BitterGit repository -> Agent workspace -> First commit
```

Hosted Bitter is designed to connect source custody to account-backed setup,
prepared workspaces, agent-run provenance, BitterGrid verification, deploys,
logs, support, and project history. Those wider services are not bundled in the
open-source server.

## Boundary

BitterGit is not a GitHub clone, project tracker, social network, CI system,
deploy executor, account/billing layer, or secret-value store.

The public `bittergit.com` root is a marketing surface, not the Git remote or
product API endpoint. The open-source service repository owns Git remotes,
repository storage, source-custody behavior, documentation, and verification
gates. The website repository owns the public site and its deployment wrapper.

## Current Status

- The open-source BitterGit alpha is public and runnable locally today.
- The integrated Bitter product can be experienced at https://bitter.sh/.
- Live website release: reported by https://bittergit.com/up

## Website Deployment Facts

- service key: `bittergit.com`
- active verified release: reported by `https://bittergit.com/up`
- health path: `/up`
- publish directory: `.output/public`
- deployment path: GitHub source event -> BitterGrid build/deploy -> Radicchio/static site

The website repository can be generated and checked with:

```bash
npm ci
npm run generate
npm run qa:smoke
npm run test:headers
Scripts/workcell-verify
```
